criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale. Include the following required information: What is the spacecraft's primary mission? Why is the mission needed? How many spacecraft are used and why? Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: Mission, rationale and single-spacecraft choice are detailed with references. Users are only partly identified: Australian facilities and scientists are implied, but operator and customers are not explicitly named. Therefore Adequate-high rather than Accomplished.

evidence.quote: The satellite, nicknamed ZYZZsat (Z-axis/Y-axis Zeroed Zoning Satellite), is operated and accessed from Australia ground facilities

criteria.name: Main body: mission design. Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate. Include relevant screenshots and software files in the main body of the report and/or appendix. Include the following information: Where will it launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? Which ground control facilities will you use? How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: Launch, orbit, ground station, duration and EOL are covered with STK screenshots and an access table. However, the SSO inclination is wrong/inconsistent with the plotted value, Kourou latitude is badly misstated, mean contact time is misreported, EOL/manoeuvre logic contradicts itself, and software files are not evidenced. criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Structure, headings and executive summary are clear, but figures/tables are inconsistently numbered or captioned, bibliography entries are mostly bare URLs without proper metadata, Wikipedia is used despite being unacceptable, and citation formatting is weak. Presentation is readable but not professional.

evidence.quote: STK 3D view of orbit: 12 hours apart

technical_issues.issue: Kourou latitude is stated as 45.05°N; actual latitude is about 5.2°N, affecting launch/inclination reasoning.
Inclination 87.79° is prograde and not sun-synchronous at 600 km; the plotted SSO value is near 97.8°, so the orbital element table is internally inconsistent.
A direct launch from Kourou at ~5°N into a ~97.8° retrograde SSO requires significant plane change/dogleg; this feasibility and cost are not assessed.
Mean access duration in the STK table is 580.786 s (about 9.7 min), not 'almost twenty minutes'; maximum is about 12.8 min.
RAAN initial value 27.33° is said to indicate the launch facility, but no launch time/geometry calculation supports this.
Text says the only manoeuvre occurs at EOL, then says the satellite has no thrusters and uses a passive drag sail; this is contradictory and the drag-sail description is incomplete.
References are largely bare URLs without titles/authors/access dates, and Wikipedia is cited despite being explicitly unacceptable.

overall: Adequately structured and covers most required mission elements, but critical orbit, launch and contact calculations are inconsistent or wrong; user/operator details are incomplete, files are not evidenced, and referencing is weak. Marks sit in the Adequate band.

feedback.summary: Your report covers most mission elements and is readable, with a clear executive summary and useful STK screenshots. The main weaknesses are orbit/launch inconsistencies, contact-time misreporting, contradictory EOL logic, incomplete user/operator detail, missing software-file evidence, and weak referencing. You are in the Adequate band; to reach Accomplished, correct these technical errors and strengthen evidence and referencing.
next_steps: Correct the launch and orbit calculations: Kourou latitude, SSO inclination consistency, RAAN/launch geometry, and the feasibility/cost of the plane change or dogleg for a retrograde SSO from ~5°N.
Reconcile the ground-contact duration with the STK table and resolve the EOL contradiction between a manoeuvre, no thrusters, and a passive drag sail; include software files as evidence.
Explicitly name the operator and customers in the Introduction, and rebuild the Bibliography with full metadata, no Wikipedia, and matching in-text citations.

criteria.C1: You clearly describe the mission, rationale and single-spacecraft choice with references. To move from Adequate to Accomplished, explicitly name the operator and customers, not just implied Australian facilities/scientists, and support user roles with literature. Your Executive Summary and Introduction already provide a good base; add specific user requirements and operational responsibilities.
criteria.C2: You cover launch, orbit, ground station, duration and EOL with STK screenshots and an access table. Next level requires correcting the Kourou latitude (45.05°N vs ~5.2°N), making the 600 km SSO inclination consistent (~97.8° retrograde, not 87.79°), assessing the plane-change/dogleg, correcting mean contact time (580.786 s ≈9.7 min, not almost 20), resolving the EOL manoeuvre/thruster/drag-sail contradiction, and evidencing software files.
criteria.C3: Your Conclusion summarises launch, orbit and ground-station choices, but it is generic and omits meaningful conclusions on mission duration and EOL. To reach Accomplished, draw specific conclusions from your evidence: state how the chosen orbit/launch/ground segment meet mission needs, justify the unbuilt Vega E with a clearer fallback, and include duration/EOL outcomes rather than only restating choices.
criteria.C4: Your structure, headings and executive summary are clear and readable. To reach Accomplished, make figure/table numbering and captions consistent (e.g. Image 1/Image 4), provide full bibliography metadata (titles, authors, access dates) instead of bare URLs, remove Wikipedia, and ensure every in-text citation matches the reference list. These changes will lift presentation from readable to professional.
